Director Naughton introduced Kirsten Graham, Public Works Manager and Wes Pringle, Deputy
Traffic Engineer.

ITEM 5A (1) – SPEED LIMIT SIGN OPTIONS

Public Works Manager Graham stated that at the City Council meeting of October 28, 2025, the
recommendation from the Traffic and Safety Committee in regard to speed limit signs was
approved. This item is coming before the Traffic and Safety Committee for recommendations on
the specifics of the signs.

Deputy Traffic Engineer Pringle stated that there are some options for the speed limit signs, as
follows:

  1. Edge-lit signs with flashing LED lights around the sign.
  2. Speed feedback signs.

Deputy Traffic Engineer Pringle stated that staff’s recommendation is to place flags on the speed
limit signs that are changing for 30 days. In addition, place an electronic message sign on Palos
Verdes Drive North at Silver Saddle to inform drivers of the change. Lastly, install permanent
edge-lit speed limit signs where the speed limit changes to 40 mph, 35 mph, and on Palos Verdes
Drive North at Ranchview Road (eastbound).

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE suggested an additional edge lit sign to be installed on Palos
Verdes Drive North just west of Crenshaw Blvd. due to the speed at which vehicles travel and the
proximity to Rancho Vista School.

A discussion ensued on the speed feedback signs; concerns were raised about their effectiveness
and cost.

The committee is in agreement with installing the three edge-lit signs.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE, Public Works Manager Graham
stated that information will be sent to the public via the City’s newsletter and social media.

COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE
to,
  INSTALL PERMANENT HIGH VISIBILITY SPEED LIMIT SIGNS IN THREE LOCATIONS
  AS PRESENTED BY STAFF.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Combs, Martin, Munday, Olson, Persichina, Rowe, Tertzakian
NOES:
ABSENT: Hall, Halvorsen, Nash
ABSTAIN:

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN
to,

   INSTALL A PERMANENT HIGH VISIBILITY SPEED LIMIT SIGN ON THE WESTBOUND
  SIDE OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH JUST WEST OF CRENSHAW BLVD.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Combs, Martin, Munday, Rowe, Tertzakian
NOES: Olson, Persichina
ABSENT: Hall, Halvorsen, Nash
ABSTAIN:

5A (2) - NO RIGHT-TURN ON RED AT THE NORTHWEST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES
DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST

Traffic Engineering Deputy Pringle stated that he observed the site and recommends installing a
“No Right-Turn on Red” on the northwest corner of Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes
Drive East for vehicles travelling southbound. This is based on the shape of the road, and visibility
issues due to a larger than normal pole and a tree.

In response to a question from CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER, Traffic Engineering Deputy Pringle
stated that due to safety issues there will be no limited hours posted; the “No Right-Turn on Red”
will be 24 hours per day.

COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON asked about any problems at that intersection in regard to safety
or accidents. Deputy Galosic stated that he does not believe there is too much of an issue;
however, he agrees with the installation of the sign due to the visibility concerns.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS stated that he has kids that go to school in the area and agrees
with the installation of the sign for safety.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS suggested putting up the electronic message board to inform
drivers about the new sign.

COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS
to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO INSTALL A NO RIGHT-
  TURN ON RED AT THE NORTHWEST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH
  AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST WITH NO RESTRICTION ON HOURS.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Combs, Martin, Munday, Olson, Persichina, Rowe, Tertzakian
NOES:
ABSENT: Hall, Halvorsen, Nash
ABSTAIN:

ITEM 5A (3) - CROSSWALK ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AT ROLLING MEADOWS
ROAD

Traffic Engineering Deputy Pringle stated that he went out to look at the site and his
recommendation is not to install a crosswalk on Palos Verdes Drive North at Rolling Meadows
Road. Typically, crosswalks are installed along with another control such as a rectangular rapid
flashing beacon or an activated signal; both are not warranted at this intersection. Since there are
no other controls, adding a crosswalk would give a false sense of security.

 A brief discussion ensued on this item.

ITEM 5A (4) - PROPOSED WAYFINDING SIGN FOR CLUB VIEW LANE ON PALOS VERDES
DRIVE EAST

Public Works Manager Graham stated that this request was made by the Rolling Hills Country
Club Estates HOA. A mock-up of the double-sided sign was presented.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE inquired about cost sharing with the HOA. Director Naughton
stated that the City has installed signs for streets that are difficult to find.

The Traffic and Safety Committee directed staff to obtain more information on the total cost of the
sign and installation.

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER recommended that the committee take a look at the improvements
to Deep Valley Drive. Public Works Manager Graham stated that there are a couple of poles and
crosswalk signs on backorder.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that there is a streetlight that has been out for years at
the entrance to the Promenade on Drybank Drive. Public Works Manager Graham stated that she
will look into it.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER adjourned the meeting at 6:40 p.m.
